report.program: Medically tailored meals, delivery and nutrition support

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

what: God's Love We Deliver cooks and delivers meals tailored to serious illness and provides nutrition support.
Its reported reach includes ill clients, children and caregivers, so our health model adjusts meal volume before estimating patient health.
The central model implies about $43.6 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Concrete cooking and delivery operations reach people unable to meet nutrition needs.
Original tax reporting supports a cost denominator with direct event costs restored.
Current geographic reporting distinguishes the five boroughs from additional counties.
reservations: A recent randomized diabetes pilot improved food security but found no differential quality-of-life or clinical improvement.
Service volume includes caregivers and children and is not a count of additional clinical benefits.
Medicaid contracts and capital expansion complicate marginal unrestricted-gift allocation.

sections.what: The recipient delivers tailored meals and dietitian support to people affected by illness. A new grocery transition program and Medicaid pathways expand the service mix. This analysis prices the whole recipient against one meal-supported health pathway, with other net health provisionally zero. [Current impact](https://www.glwd.org/about-us/2025-impact-summary-report/) [Healthcare partnerships](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.monitoring:
A 74-person randomized Maryland diabetes pilot used 12 meals weekly for 3 months plus dietitian calls. It reduced food insecurity, but clinical and diabetes-quality-of-life changes did not differ between arms at 6 months. This challenges translating meals into large health gains. Our 0.01 utility coefficient is a small subjective positive scenario, not a measured effect from that study; zero health remains plausible. [Original trial](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-024-09248-x)

Request residence, distinct clinical recipients, meals actually consumed, days exposed and controlled utility outcomes. Do not add hospitalization savings, reported satisfaction or meal counts as separate QALYs.
sections.qualitative: Home delivery may reduce physical burden and nutritional instability for people with complex illness. Alternative family support, other meal programs and insurance-funded nutrition remain available to varying degrees. Grocery transition and Medicaid expansion change the marginal service mix; it is not established that an unrestricted gift buys the historical average bundle. [Partner pathways](https://www.glwd.org/healthcare-partnerships/)
sections.cost: The model starts with FY2024 tax functional expense $49,631,474 and restores $2,377,336 direct fundraising-event costs plus $10,034 inventory cost netted outside that total, giving $52,018,844 recipient resources. A 1.1 forward multiplier gives $57,220,728.40. Benefit uses 4.2 million meals/624 meals per patient-year, 0.8 clinical-patient meal share, 0.5 incremental nutrition over alternatives, 0.01 utility gain, 0.5 gift additionality and 0.975 MSA share: 13.125 MSA QALYs. Price is $43,596,745 per 10. Exposure is volume-limited and capped at one year per client; no survival benefit or post-service continuation is credited. Volunteer time and external medical spending are excluded, so this is not full social cost effectiveness.
sections.funding:
The operating recipient's FY2024 return spans July 1, 2023–June 30, 2024. It reports $42,055,419 program, $2,084,720 management and $5,491,335 fundraising functional costs. Programs include a food festival, so food/delivery direct costs alone would understate the recipient. The same return records 4.2 million meals and 15,839 clients/caregivers/children. [Original Form 990, pages 1–2, 9–10](https://e1.nmcdn.io/assets/glwd/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Gods-Love-We-Deliver-Public-Disclosure-Copy-5-15-25.pdf)

For a $1,000 gift, scaling the whole recipient's forward cost corresponds to about 73 historical meal units before marginal-capacity and clinical adjustments; this is a portfolio equivalent, not a promised meal purchase. Public/insurance contracts and other fundraising continue; b=.5 discounts substitution. Current giving accepts ordinary gifts, with no verified restricted incremental offer. [Donation route](https://www.glwd.org/donate/)

The current 2025 impact page instead reports 3,689,816 meals and 15,115 people including children and caregivers. This model deliberately pairs FY2024 output with FY2024 expense before its assumed forward-cost multiplier; it is not a measured 2025 cost-effectiveness result. Substituting 2025 volume while retaining projected cost gives 11.530675 MSA QALYs and about $49.6 million per 10; this sensitivity does not repair the missing current expense.

model.costScope: FY2024 recipient functional expenses plus direct fundraising-event and inventory costs netted against revenue; all programs retained including festival; multiplied1.1 for forward cost. Volunteer time and outside clinical costs excluded.
model.geographicAttribution: 2025 distribution reports95% across NYC five boroughs,5% Hudson/Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester/Monroe combined. First four are MSA counties; MonroeNY is outside (MonroePA is inside). Without split/state detail set g=.975, sensitivity .95–1. Transfer of2025 geography to2024-volume projection explicit.
model.formula: C=F+E+I; exposure=min(M/D,N)*r; Q_all=exposure*a*u*b; Q_MSA=Q_all*g; cost=C*f; price10=10*cost/Q_MSA. D=12*52meal units per supported-year; N caps at one-year per reported recipient; clinical share r; additional nutrition a; utility u; funding b.
model.counterfactual: Ordinary public/private contracts, other donors, other meal providers and family food continue. a=.5 discounts alternative nutrition; b=.5 separately discounts financing substitution. No healthcare savings are converted into additional QALYs.
model.attribution: Model follows unrestricted recipient portfolio. r=.8 removes caregiver/child meal units from the illness-utility calculation rather than valuing all recipients as ill adults. Nutrition counseling assumed included in utility, not added.
model.uncertainty: Very weak causal and marginal estimate. Randomized pilot's null quality-of-life contrast makes zero material. Gift allocation, meal intensity and source-year transfer may dominate observed food volume.
model.nativeOutcomes: Dose-equivalent patient-years of incremental nutrition while services occur; finite utility only, mortality zero.

inputs.name: F
inputs.rationale: Whole-recipient Form990 PartIX total including depreciation.

inputs.name: E
inputs.rationale: PartVIII line8b, excluded from PartIX; restored without double counting festival program expenses.

inputs.name: I
inputs.rationale: PartVIII line10b, netted from revenue; restored.

inputs.name: M
inputs.rationale: FY2024 rounded report count; not2025 output.

inputs.name: D
inputs.rationale: 12 weekly meals ×52; trial dose is a reference intensity, not proof a full-year exposure occurred.

inputs.name: N
inputs.rationale: Exposure cap prevents lifetime multiplication or more than one year per individual.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: 20% removed for caregiver/child meals; no clinical outcome assumed for those meals.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: Half of nutritional support assumed available from alternatives.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: Small subjective positive gain; pilot RCT does not establish it and zero is plausible.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Half discounted for replacement funding and capacity constraints.

inputs.name: g
inputs.rationale: 95%explicit boroughs plus half of pooled5%; state/county uncertainty remains.

sensitivity: Zero utility yields zero QALYs regardless of meal output; small positive utility is not established by the cited randomized pilot.
g=.95–1 changes geographic price only modestly; changing b=.5 to.1 multiplies price5fold.
Changing D624 to1040 (20meals weekly) reduces dose-equivalent patient-years40%; future expenses2x historical without more output doubles price relative to f=1.
Net health harms of13.125 geographic QALYs erase the central benefit; dietary adverse effects and displaced care are not measured.

Current-volume sensitivity: replacing M=4200000 and N=15839 with 2025 M=3689816 and N=15115, holding all other central assumptions, gives 11.530675 MSA QALYs and $49,624,787 per 10. This is a cross-year sensitivity, not a matched current-year estimate.
